issues.legal_issue: For a suit seeking specific performance of an agreement that fixes a date for performance, limitation runs from the fixed date, as extended by an agreed extension, and is not postponed by delivery of possession, pending permission, or a later allegation of avoidance.
material_facts: The written agreement fixed a date for execution of the sale deed, and the sellers later sought extensions to obtain the lessor’s permission; the last requested extension expired on 1 February 1977.
The buyer had received possession when the agreement was made, and the permission remained unobtained.
The buyer alleged that the sellers began avoiding the buyer after August 1991 and that the cause of action was continuing, but filed suit in April 1994.
The plaint did not give particulars of any alleged oral extension of time.
issues.conclusion: The suit was barred by limitation because it was filed more than three years after the final date fixed for performance; possession, the unobtained permission, and the later allegation of avoidance did not defer or renew the limitation period.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 54 of the Limitation Act, a suit for specific performance must be filed within three years from the date fixed for performance; where no date is fixed, time runs from when the claimant has notice that performance is refused. Delivery of possession does not alter the limitation rule, and failure to obtain permission does not by itself postpone the cause of action. The judgment does not rely on an earlier decision in its reasoning.

rule.if: specific_performance_suit and performance_date_fixed and final_extension_expired and filing_followed_expired_limitation_window and buyer_received_possession and permission_remained_unobtained and later_avoidance_alleged and later_extension_lacked_particulars

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The claimant brought a suit seeking specific performance of an agreement to sell.
predicates.performance_date_fixed: The agreement fixed a date for performance.
predicates.final_extension_expired: The last extension sought for performance expired.
predicates.filing_followed_expired_limitation_windo: The claimant filed suit after the applicable limitation period had elapsed from the final performance date.
predicates.buyer_received_possession: The seller delivered possession to the buyer when the agreement was made.
predicates.permission_remained_unobtained: Permission needed for the transaction remained unobtained.
predicates.later_avoidance_alleged: The claimant alleged that the seller later avoided the claimant.
predicates.later_extension_lacked_particulars: The claimant alleged a further oral extension without stating when it was given or how long it lasted.

issues.definition: When a specific-performance suit follows a fixed performance date and expired final extension by more than the applicable limitation period, the claim is time-barred even if possession was delivered, permission remained pending, and later avoidance was alleged without particulars of a further extension.

issues.legal_issue: A plaint may be rejected at the threshold when its own averments show that a suit for specific performance is barred by limitation.
material_facts: The defendants applied for rejection of the plaint on the ground that the suit was time-barred.
The plaint stated the agreement’s fixed performance date, the requested extensions and their final expiry, and the later date on which the suit was filed.
The trial court rejected the plaint as barred by limitation, but the High Court reversed that order; the Supreme Court restored the trial court’s order.
issues.conclusion: The plaint was properly rejected because its averments showed that the suit was barred by limitation.
issues.legal_principle: Order VII Rule 11(a) and (d) of the Code of Civil Procedure requires the court to consider whether the plaint discloses a cause of action and whether it appears to be barred by law. Read with Article 54 of the Limitation Act, the plaint’s own dates showed that the specific-performance suit was time-barred. The judgment does not rely on an earlier decision in its reasoning.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The claimant brought a suit seeking specific performance of an agreement to sell.
predicates.plaint_rejection_sought: The opposing party applied for rejection of the plaint.
predicates.plaint_dates_show_limitation_bar: The dates and other averments stated in the plaint show that the applicable limitation period had elapsed before the suit was filed.

issues.definition: If a party seeks rejection of a plaint in a specific-performance suit and the plaint’s own averments show that the limitation period elapsed before filing, the plaint is rejected.
